text:
alex: ran a short experiment on s1-gpu with a probabilistic wait stratification to trade a bit of latency for larger microbatches. idea: for small requests (<64 tokens) sample an extra wait from an exponential("mu"=4ms) capped by max_wait_ms so we only delay a subset of mini-requests and avoid regressing p95 too much.

maria: can you paste the exact config you used?

alex: config snippet:
```
max_batch_tokens: 1024
max_wait_ms: 8
prob_wait_threshold_tokens: 64
prob_wait_lambda_ms: 4.0
max_extra_wait_ms: 6
kernel_preference: ["fused", "fallback"]
```

cheng: cool — what changed in the metrics?

alex: baseline (no-prob-wait): p50=22ms p95=48ms p99=210ms throughput=220rps kv_hit=89% fused_util=13%
prob-wait (single-run): p50=24ms p95=52ms p99=160ms throughput=270rps kv_hit=85% fused_util=31%

maria: wow p99 drop is solid, throughput up. but kv_hit down a bit, any idea why?

alex: looks like reordering: delaying small token requests increases chance they coalesce but also means some requests hit before their KV caches warm up (cold KV lookups land at tail). saw a couple of long KV miss latencies in traces.

ana: did kernel distribution change — more fused path?

alex: yes fused increased from ~13% -> ~31%. so kernel selection benefited from fuller batches, but KV misses dominate the tail when they occur inside a large batch.

jordan: can you drop a log sample?

alex: log snippet:
```
[2025-11-02T11:02:12Z] req=3124 tokens=40 wait_ms=5 dispatched=fused kv_hit=false latency=178ms
[2025-11-02T11:02:12Z] req=3125 tokens=512 wait_ms=0 dispatched=fallback kv_hit=true latency=46ms
```

maria: makes sense. if small requests probabilistically wait, some will hit hot cache later, some will suffer. Have we tried biasing waits by predicted kv_hit probability?

cheng: we already compute a per-route kv_hit estimator in profiler. could apply smaller lambda when kv_miss_prob > 0.1.

alex: tried a simple adaptive rule: if recent kv_miss_rate > 10% reduce prob_wait_lambda to 1ms (from 4ms). result: p95 ~50ms p99 ~140ms throughput 260rps kv_hit ~87%. so better tail while keeping throughput gains.

perf-bot: regression check: p99 improved >10% and p95 within 20% -> suppressed alert.

jordan: any interaction with max_batch_tokens? I worry larger max_batch_tokens could amplify KV-miss tails.

alex: we did a run with max_batch_tokens=2048: throughput +15% but p99 rose (edge cases) because KV miss inside big batches caused long per-token queues.

maria: propose A/B: route 10% traffic to prob-wait with kv-aware lambda and collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, kv_hit_rate, fused_util, avg_batch_tokens, tail_>300ms_count.

ana: I'll add trace tags: kv_hit, kernel, batch_size, wait_ms, route. also add span for KV lookup time.

cheng: small operational concern — router head-of-line blocking. if we artificially delay many small requests, ensure per-worker max_inflight_tokens prevents single worker getting overloaded. add guard: max_inflight_tokens=65536.

alex: agreed. will open an experiment ticket with metrics to collect and the rollout plan. also will include a fallback: if p99 > 200ms in canary, rollback immediately.

maria: please include kernel switch profiling (time spent in fused vs fallback, occupancy) — we want to confirm fused still wins overall for cost/latency. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: prob-wait A/B rollout -> canary=10% start=2025-11-03T09:00Z (automated monitors attached).

jordan: thanks — also add a dashboard widget that slices p99 by kv_hit=true/false so we can see tail contribution.

alex: will do and will post results in #eng-runtime by EOD Friday.

maria: :raised_hands: good work, putting this on the perf board for follow-up.
